title: economy-sentinel: prefetch conductor + compact-quant-fuse adapter
author: Elena Torres
description:
Motivation: We see recurring tenant cold-start costs driven by inefficient prefill behavior and conservative quant-profile fallbacks. Teams repeatedly tune tenant defaults per-product which is slow and error-prone. This PR introduces 'economy-sentinel', a prefetch conductor that coordinates lightweight prefill decisions across tenants and a compact-quant-fuse adapter that automatically maps workload signatures to a small set of vetted quant profiles. The intent is to reduce unit econ volatility while preserving tail latency and output quality.

What this change does: - Adds a prefill conductor (pkg/prefill/conductor.go) that centralizes prefetch policies, applies hedged prefetch (light weight, latency-aware), and emits tenant-level prefill telemetry for the Console. - Introduces compact quant-fuse selector (pkg/quant/fuse_selector.py + services/quant/adapter.go) which evaluates signature histograms and selects a ranked list of 3 compact quant profiles (int8/4-bit hybrid) with safety fallbacks. - Exposes a small CLI tool (cli/costctl) to dry-run economy-sentinel recommendations against historical traces for unit-econ estimates. - Adds a lightweight sampler-based simulator (tests/bench/prefill_sim.py) that produces synthetic tenant traces used in automated regression checks. - Adds docs and an RFC (docs/rfc/economy-sentinel.md) describing tradeoffs and rollout plan.

Implementation notes: - Prefetch decisions are decoupled from runtime serving threads; conductor runs as a sidecar-style service and publishes scored prefill actions via the existing routing pub/sub; action schema is intentionally small to keep overhead sub-millisecond. - The quant-fuse selector uses a compact signature fingerprint (token length distribution + prefix-match entropy) computed at inference time and batched to the adapter. Adapter returns ranked quant profiles and an estimated quality delta computed from stored evals; conservative fallback stays on fp16/32 when quality delta is > threshold. - Cost estimates use the same unit-cost model in Optimize but add a small safety multiplier for cold-prefetch to avoid over-optimistic recommendations.

Testing and CI: Unit tests for conductor state machine, adapter profile ranking, and CLI dry-run added. Integration bench sim validates end-to-end prefetch -> warmed-cache hit rate and unit-econ delta. Perf bench shows median latency impact < 1.2% on 2048-sequence workloads with up to 18% reduction in token cost for cold-heavy tenants in our synthetic tests. CI flakiness observed in initial e2e networking test (intermittent port binding) and fixed by adding backoff and ephemeral port allocation.

Rollout: Feature flags added (prefill.conductor.enabled, quant.adapter.enabled). Default off for all tenants; opt-in via console for customers to collect telemetry for 2 weeks. Gradual rollout: start with internal tenants -> canary customers -> broad opt-in.

Related: ENG-1428 (prefetch coordination), ENG-1503 (quant profile safety), SUP-9081 (customer incident that motivated safer prefilling).

Checklist: - [x] Prefetch conductor implementation - [x] Compact quant-fuse adapter - [x] CLI dry-run and cost estimator - [x] Bench simulator and unit tests - [x] Docs and RFC - [x] Feature flags and rollout plan

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the quant profile set small (3 profiles) to limit combinatorial explosion during rollouts. The conductor will respect tenant-level guardrails and will never trigger aggressive prefill for tenants marked sensitive in their policy.

ci_checks: perf-bench: pass (median latency +1.1%, cost -14% on cold-heavy tenant sim)
release_notes: Introduce economy-sentinel prefetch conductor and compact-quant-fuse adapter. Admins can opt-in to conservative prefetch recommendations and use CLI dry-run to estimate unit-econ impact. Feature is behind flags and rolled out gradually.
short_summary: Centralized prefetch conductor + automated compact quant profile selector to lower cold-start unit costs while protecting latency and quality.
risk_assessment: Medium: changes touch prefill decision path and quant selection. Mitigations: feature flags, small profile set, conservative thresholds, tenant policy guardrails, and canary rollout.
rollout_plan: Enable flags for internal tenants for 2 weeks, monitor prefill hit-rate & unit-econ delta, canary to 5 customers for 1 week, then broad opt-in. Immediate rollback via feature flag or disable adapter service.
test_plan: Unit tests for state machine and ranking, integration test for sensitive-policy exemption, perf bench comparing warmed-cache hit rates, CLI dry-run reproducibility tests against stored traces. All added to CI.
notes_for_maintainers: When backporting to release branches keep the feature-flag wiring separate; do not enable by default. The helm configmap includes the tunables and defaults under 'prefill' namespace.
